issues.failure_explanation: The eigenfunctions of eq:EVP span only H^2∩H^1_0, yet the theorem is invoked for sound hard/impedance where X=H^2(Omega); the expansion of an arbitrary u in X is invalid. The statement is actually false there: on the infinite-dimensional closed subspace of harmonic H^2 functions, A reduces to (grad u,grad v)-k^2(u,v); a weakly null H^2-normalised harmonic sequence tends to 0 in H^1, so no inf-sup/T-coercivity in H^2 holds. The discrete impedance case repeats this (T_h on X_h, eigenfunctions only in X~_h∩H^1_0).

issues.failure_explanation: Functions in H^2∩H^1_0 have nonzero normal derivatives, so integrations by parts leave boundary terms; fourth derivatives of H^2 functions are also not available. On a flat boundary piece {y=0}, (u_xy,v_yy)-(u_yy,v_xy) equals the integral of u_y d_x(v_y), an antisymmetric, generally nonzero term. Thus e(u,v)-e(v,u) is nonzero whenever n_x n_y ≠ 0 (e.g. diagonal director on the square). The expansion coefficient (n_x+n_y)^2 should also be 1.
